channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Swiss Franc loses ground upbeat US Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: USD/CHF trades higher on Friday as stronger-than-expected United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data trigger fresh volatility. The pair jumped to 0.8126 following the release before giving back part of its advance. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8102, up nearly 0.34% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Gradual improvement outlook on labour market – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan notes Canada’s labour market lost 42,000 jobs in August, partly reversing earlier gains and leaving modest year-to-date job growth. She emphasizes structural factors like demographics and weaker immigration as key drags.

item.title: United States: Solid jobs data support steady Fed – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Christoph Balz notes that the U.S. labor market surprised to the upside in August, with Nonfarm Payrolls and private sector jobs both rising strongly while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Wage growth continued to slow.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike path and oil risks – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global Markets Research team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak, George Buckley and Josie Anderson, expects the ECB to raise the depo rate by 25bp to 2.50% at the 10 September meeting and then pause.

item.title: "Lower the rate or I’ll stop trading": Trump pressures Fed after strong US jobs report
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, United States (US) President Donald Trump welcomed the creation of 162K jobs in August, a figure he described as significantly above expectations.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs weakness caps gains against US Dollar - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Canada’s softer August labour report, including weaker employment momentum and slower wage growth, is unlikely to materially change the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) assessment of the labour market.

item.title: Canadian Dollar slides as Canada sheds 41.7K jobs, US payrolls surge
item.description: USD/CAD accelerates sharply higher on Friday, trading around 1.3850 at the time of writing, up 0.39% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Jobs strength lifts hike odds – ING
item.description: ING’s James Knightley notes that stronger-than-expected US August jobs data, with 162,000 new positions and upward revisions, has increased the perceived likelihood of a September Federal Reserve rate hike.

item.title: British Pound trims losses against US Dollar after NFP-driven volatility
item.description: GBP/USD recovers part of its initial drop on Friday after stronger-than-expected United States (US) employment data briefly lifts the US Dollar (USD). The pair fell to an intraday low of 1.3482 immediately after the release before rebounding. At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades around 1.3512.

item.title: Gold: Central bank buying underpins prices – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that central banks, led by China and Poland, continued net Gold purchases in July, supporting structural demand despite a slower pace than last year.

item.title: Euro slips against US Dollar as Nonfarm Payrolls crush expectations
item.description: EUR/USD comes under selling pressure on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens following the release of the upbeat United States (US) employment report. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1605, down roughly 0.18% on the day, after retreating from an intraday high of 1.1633.

item.title: Japanese Yen steadies against US Dollar after strong NFP report
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 155.85 on Friday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day.

item.title: Gold tumbles as blockbuster US NFP lift US Dollar, Treasury yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) falls sharply on Friday, snapping a two-day recovery after the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report surprised strongly to the upside. The metal briefly climbed above $4,500 on Thursday, gaining nearly 2%, but has since erased a large part of that advance.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Trade talks support Peso against US Dollar - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale reports that USD/MXN has moved back below 17.00 as Mexican officials engage with US counterparts on trade issues following a widening US-Canada rift. The bank highlights a sharp drop in Mexico’s car imports from China after tariff adjustments aimed at protecting local jobs.

item.title: Euro retreats against Pound Sterling as Eurozone Retail Sales disappoint
item.description: EUR/GBP trades on the back foot on Friday, snapping a four-day winning streak that pushed the cross above 0.8600 to its highest level since July 1. Softer-than-expected Eurozone Retail Sales data weighs modestly on the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Breaking: US Nonfarm Payrolls rise by 162K in August vs. 56K forecast
item.description: Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) in the United States (US) rose by 162K in August, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Friday. This print followed July's increase of 21K and surpassed the market expectation of 56K by a wide margin.

item.title: European Central Bank: Inflation-driven hike prospects – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to raise the deposit facility rate to 2.50%, citing a resilient inflation-growth mix in the Eurozone. The report notes headline inflation has moved further above target, while core pressures remain contained for now.

item.title: WTI Oil retreats below $89 despite persistent tensions around the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil declines 1.21% on Friday and trades around $88.55 per barrel at the time of writing.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Close call on further tightening – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Christoph Balz expects the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged, but highlights a significant risk of another 25 bps hike.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Sharp rebound and Fed repricing – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan highlights a sharp strengthening in the Japanese Yen, with USD/JPY dropping from 160 to around 155.30 as the Dollar broadly weakened and Asian FX gained.

item.title: United States Dollar Index edges higher to near 99.00 ahead of US NFP data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is marginally up on Friday ahead of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for August, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD trapped below 100-day SMA as US NFP approaches
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) consolidates with marginal losses on Friday following back-to-back daily gains, as traders avoid taking large positions ahead of the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: Canadian Dollar steadies at 1.3800 awaiting employment data from US and Canada
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) holds minor losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as the USD/CAD pair trades just above 1.3800 after bouncing from two-week lows at 1.3765.

item.title: Indian Rupee outperforms amid strong foreign inflows in FCNR (B) deposits
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) jumps almost 1% higher against the US Dollar (USD) this week. On Friday, the USD/INR pair trades close to its two-month low of 94.29 posted the previous day.

item.title: US Dollar: Short-term downside risks – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that dovish comments from Federal Reserve official Christopher Waller have pushed US yields and the Dollar lower, while supporting equities and high-yielding FX.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: On track to revisit four-year high near 0.7280
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades marginally higher at around 0.7203 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The Aussie pair is broadly firm as the US Dollar remains under pressure, with traders reassessing Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate expectations.

item.title: British Pound pulls back from session highs as BoE Bailey tames rate hike hopes
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) has retreated from session highs just below 1.3550 against the US Dollar (USD) during the London trading session, returning to levels near 1.3520 and turning negative on the daily chart.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher vs Yen as RBA tightening bets meet BoJ normalization hopes
item.description: AUD/JPY advances on Friday and trades around 112.65 at the time of writing, up 0.39% on the day.

item.title: BoE's Bailey defends central bank flexibility, warns of bond market pressures
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Governor Andrew Bailey said on Friday that monetary policymakers have some discretion over how quickly they bring inflation back to target, while stressing that returning inflation to the target remains imperative.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Data volatility guides Bank of Canada – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts Norman Liebke and Michael Pfister report that the Bank of Canada kept its policy rate at 2.25% but adopted a more hawkish tone as inflation risks rise from higher energy prices and trade tensions with the US.
